claims.claim: AC1: Repository policy defaults are exactly Codex gpt-6-sol/medium and Antigravity gemini-3.8-flash/medium, and the preserved candidate proves the policy remains the sole default authority with no adapter/carrier/workflow duplicate default constants.

AC2: Local run and continue, including continue delegation into PRIMARY, REMEDIATION, and coding REPAIR, accept partial or complete Human model/effort overrides for Codex/Antigravity; direct canonical REMEDIATION and coding REPAIR surfaces preserve the same semantics. Omitted dimensions resolve deterministically, EXPLICIT versus REPOSITORY_DEFAULT attribution is preserved, and the exact resolved values reach native command construction.

AC3: A new authorization never implicitly inherits the previous RUN profile, while replay/restart/reconciliation of the same authorization reuses its exact bound profile even after repository defaults change.

AC4: PRIMARY remote carrier v3 validates one exact Human request, resolves one exact profile from canonical policy, propagates it through self-host delivery, and binds it into a new profile-aware durable PRIMARY dispatch identity before RUN native execution.

AC5: REMEDIATION intent v2 and REPAIR wakeup v2 provide the same exact request-resolution, workflow propagation, durable dispatch binding, idempotent replay, and changed-profile collision rejection guarantees as PRIMARY.

AC6: New profile-aware dispatch records and the eventual per-RUN execution-profile sidecar agree exactly on executor/model/effort/source attribution; any disagreement or invalid profile fails before native invocation.

AC7: Historical PRIMARY v1/v2, REMEDIATION v1, and REPAIR v1 durable journals remain readable/reconcilable under their exact historical semantics. Replaying or reconciling one of those existing identities does not resolve, attach, compare against, or persist current repository defaults, does not upgrade the journal version, and does not fabricate execution-profile provenance or a new native authorization. Newly submitted legacy carrier request versions are rejected rather than silently applying current defaults.

AC8: Invalid effort, malformed model identifier, missing required Executor/profile context, and profile options supplied to MiniMax invoke zero native Executors; MiniMax execution without profile options remains behaviorally unchanged.

AC9: A syntactically valid explicit alternate/future provider-native model identifier can flow end-to-end through local and remote profile binding without source-code registration or a global allowlist. Native provider rejection remains a no-fallback execution failure.

AC10: Remote operational receipts can retain bounded exact profile selectors where relevant without becoming lifecycle truth, and existing carrier receipts still avoid asserting RUN/verification/review/publication success from workflow completion alone.

AC11: Frozen TASK/RUN/RunLease/ExecutorBoundary semantics, Dispatcher exactly-one selection, sandbox/mutation authority, Runtime verification/EVIDENCE, Reviewer, Publisher, and no-retry/no-reroute boundaries remain unchanged.

AC12: Focused regression proves that after TASK-163 a compatible future default change can be expressed by editing only repository profile policy plus focused validation/smoke, with no required adapter, Dispatcher, Human carrier schema, durable dispatch schema, or lifecycle redesign. Adapter-mechanics regressions exercise explicitly injected profiles rather than duplicating the current repository default values as a second default authority.
